# Narrative Quality Checklist: Narrative Overview Page

**Purpose**: Test whether the spec and plan define "the Overview reads well" precisely enough to write tasks against and to judge generated prose. Covers explanation-first structure, grounding and traceability, tone and style, length, link routing, generated-text marking, and the degraded page.
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [research.md](../research.md) · [contract](../contracts/overview-narrative.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Audience / timing**: reviewer, before `/speckit-tasks`. **Depth**: standard. Scope: User Stories 1, 2 and 4 (the first release); User Story 3 only where it shares a rule.

## Explanation-First Structure

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the minimum length of the lead stated consistently? US1's story text and scenario 1 require "between two and four paragraphs", while the "single subsystem" edge case allows "down to a single paragraph" and FR-005 sets only a maximum. [Conflict, Spec §US1-AS1, §FR-005, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK002 - Does the spec say which job each lead paragraph does, and in what order, beyond "the first says what the repository is"? Is a lead that names subsystems but never describes flow a failure of FR-005? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §US1-AS2]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is "what the repository is and does, in its own terms" defined? Does "its own terms" mean the repository's own vocabulary, its README's framing, or its code's names? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is "where work enters the system and where its results end up" defined for repositories with several independent entry points, such as a frontend and a backend, or a CLI and an HTTP API? Must the lead describe one flow, the principal one, or all of them? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005, §US1-AS4]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for a repository with no identifiable entry point (a library, a docs-only repository), where "where work enters" has no referent? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is it specified how many of the major subsystems the lead must name? SC-001 expects a reader to name at least three, but FR-005 only says "name its major subsystems". [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is the placement of the repository-facts block relative to the lead stated in the spec, and not only in the contract outline? FR-001 says "ahead of every list", and the facts block is a list. [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Contract §6]
- [ ] CHK008 - After User Story 2, are the Overview's section headings and their order specified, so that "same headings with and without provider" (FR-014) has a fixed reference outline to compare against? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-021–025]

## Grounding & Traceability

- [ ] CHK009 - Does the spec define what counts as "naming" a file, module or symbol? Is a descriptive phrase such as "the lending service" a name subject to FR-009, or only an identifier? The plan's G5 draws this line, but the spec does not. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009, Plan research D6]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are requirements stated for the accuracy of **relational** claims ("A calls B", "work passes from X to Y"), which can be false while every name in them exists? Or is existence the whole grounding bar, with relations left to SC-001 review? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is FR-009–FR-013's scope consistent with the table? The Responsibility column carries planner-written subsystem descriptions, which are generated text on the Overview, yet the plan grounds and style-checks only the narrator's paragraphs. [Conflict, Spec §FR-009, §FR-013, §FR-021, Plan research D10]
- [ ] CHK012 - Does constitution §2.4, "every AI answer is traceable to source fragments", hold for a lead paragraph whose only anchor is a subsystem link, which is a page and not a source fragment? Is FR-007's "one link to a subsystem or module page" intended to satisfy §2.4? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Constitution §2.4]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the edge case "does not repeat claims about things that are absent from the code" measurable? Can a reviewer tell a README-derived purpose claim that is fine from one about absent features? [Measurability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is FR-009's "at the analysed revision" defined for a working tree with uncommitted changes, where the analysed content differs from the recorded commit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is it specified whether the lead may reproduce sentences from the repository's own documentation verbatim, which could import its promotional wording, or must paraphrase? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, Edge Cases]

## Tone & Style

- [ ] CHK016 - Is present tense verifiable anywhere in the success criteria? FR-013 assigns it to "the human review in SC-001", but SC-001 measures subsystem recall and entry-point identification, not tense. [Measurability, Conflict, Spec §FR-013, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is the scope of the banned list defined: adjectives only, or also adverbs ("seamlessly", "easily", "simply") and noun phrases ("state of the art")? Who owns changes to the list, and where is it recorded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Assumptions, Plan data-model Constants]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are hedging and speculative forms ("likely", "appears to", "probably", "may be used for") addressed? They contradict "declarative" but match no current rule. [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK019 - Is "no marketing adjectives" given a test beyond the banned list, for evaluative words not on it ("efficient", "comprehensive")? Or is the list declared exhaustive for the purpose of SC-009? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013, §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK020 - Is the intended reader defined: a developer new to the repository, or a non-developer? Are expectations stated for jargon, acronyms and a term's first use? [Gap, Spec §SC-001]

## Length Limits

- [ ] CHK021 - Is the counting basis for "under 600 words" defined? Do backticked code names and subsystem links count as rendered, where a handle expands to a multi-word title, or as the model wrote them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005a, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is "sentence" defined for the three-sentence cap on subsystem paragraphs, given abbreviations ("e.g.") and dotted names (`pkg.module`)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-025, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is it specified which prose is removed first when a length limit is exceeded, or is "MUST NOT be published as written" left to the plan (G9 trims subsystem paragraphs last-first, then lead paragraphs)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005a, Plan research D6]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is the relationship between the four-paragraph lead cap and a per-paragraph length stated? Could four very long paragraphs meet FR-005 while defeating "an overview that needs scrolling twice isn't one"? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, Clarifications Q5]

## Link Routing

- [ ] CHK025 - Does a link to a symbol anchor on a module page count as "a link to a subsystem or module page" for FR-007? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK026 - Is link density bounded, or considered at all? Every backticked name becomes a link, so a paragraph can be mostly links. [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is it required that a subsystem's link text in the prose is its current title as shown in the navigation, so the lead and sidebar never call the same subsystem by two names? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK028 - Is "ends with a link to that subsystem's page" (FR-025) defined as the paragraph's final element, or only as containing such a link near the end? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, §US2-AS4]

## Generated-Text Marking

- [ ] CHK029 - Is the unit of marking specified: one marked block for the whole lead, or one marker per paragraph? The plan chooses a merged block; the spec is silent. [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Plan research D10]
- [ ] CHK030 - After User Story 1 ships alone, is the existing Features list (subsystem title and planner-written description, currently unmarked) required to be marked, or removed? Otherwise FR-012 is violated until User Story 2 lands. [Conflict, Spec §FR-012, §US1 independence, Plan story map]
- [ ] CHK031 - Is "legible in both light and dark appearance" quantified, for example with a contrast ratio as spec 037 used (4.5:1)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK032 - Is the generated marker required to be perceivable non-visually (assistive technology), or is visual marking alone intended? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK033 - Is the table-header marking rule stated for a mix of rows where some descriptions are generated and some are not, and for a table whose rows are all empty? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012 (amended), §FR-021]

## Degraded & No-Provider Page

- [ ] CHK034 - Are requirements defined for a **partially** grounded lead, such as when the opening "what the repository is" paragraph is rejected but later ones survive, leaving a lead that starts mid-story? Is the lead then kept, reordered or dropped? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-010, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK035 - Is uneven subsystem coverage specified, where some major subsystems get a paragraph and others lose theirs to grounding? Is a section with gaps acceptable, or must it be all or none? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK036 - Is FR-018's reporting requirement stated for partial drops, not only for full omission and fallback? The contract adds "k of n paragraphs dropped"; the spec does not. [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, Contract §7]
- [ ] CHK037 - Is it specified what a repository that has changed shows when no provider can answer? Should the last narrative whose names still resolve be kept, or should the prose disappear until a provider answers? The plan implies the latter because the key changes. [Gap, Recovery, Spec §FR-014, §FR-017, Plan research D7]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is it an intended requirement, or an incidental property, that a narrative produced earlier is shown when no provider is available on a later unchanged run? FR-015 conditions identity on "the same providers available". [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015, §FR-016, Contract §2]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK039 - Is SC-001's review protocol defined: how many reviewers, what counts as "correctly" naming a subsystem (title, or a synonym), and what counts as the correct starting point in a repository with several entry points? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK040 - Is the "verification set" used by SC-002, SC-007 and SC-009 defined: which repositories, and which fabricated or adversarial replies (unbackticked names, handles for missing subsystems, Markdown injection)? [Completeness, Spec §SC-002, §SC-007, §SC-009]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK041 - Is narrative quality addressed for the case where subsystem titles are the planner's plain fallback names (directory-derived, such as "services" or "impl")? The lead links and names subsystems by those titles, and reads accordingly. [Assumption, Dependency on spec 033, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK042 - Is the dependency on subsystem descriptions (spec 033's one-sentence planner output) as the table's Responsibility column recorded with its failure mode, an empty "—" for every unplanned subsystem? [Dependency, Spec §FR-021, Clarifications Q1]
